label: Beginner
blurb: The words and phrases you hear every single day — greetings, the daily schedule, and the handful of replies that get you through a hallway conversation.
blurbZh: 每天一定聽得到的字詞：問候語、作息時間、走廊上最常用的回應。

questions.q: A child points at you and says 老師. They are calling you —
questions.why: 老師 (lǎoshī) is the everyday word for teacher. Students use it as a title all by itself — just 老師, no name attached.

questions.q: A student bows slightly in the hallway and says 老師好. The most natural response is —
opts: Ask them to say it in English
Smile and say 你好 (nǐ hǎo)
questions.why: 老師好 is a greeting, not a question. A smile plus 你好 (nǐ hǎo) or just 早 (zǎo) is all anyone expects.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. What is being said?
questions.why: 早安 (zǎo'ān) = good morning. Around campus you will hear the shorter 早 (zǎo) even more often.

questions.py: nǐ yào bú yào yìqǐ chī biàndāng?
questions.q: At noon a colleague asks 你要不要一起吃便當？They are inviting you to —
questions.why: 便當 (biàndāng) is the boxed lunch most school staff eat together at their desks. Sharing one is the everyday way colleagues include you.

questions.q: The speakers announce 打掃時間. Students across campus will now —
questions.why: 打掃時間 (dǎsǎo shíjiān) is the daily cleaning period. Every class has an assigned zone, and teachers usually supervise.

questions.q: A homeroom teacher says 辛苦了 to you after a long class. They mean —
questions.why: 辛苦了 (xīnkǔ le) acknowledges someone's effort. It is a compliment, not a comment on how tired you look.

questions.q: 上課 means —
opts: class is starting / to be in class
questions.why: 上課 (shàngkè) = to start class or to be in class. Its opposite is 下課 (xiàkè), the break.

questions.q: When you hear 下課, students are about to —
questions.why: 下課 (xiàkè) is the break between periods — usually 10 minutes. 下班 (xiàbān) is the staff equivalent, finishing work.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. What is being said?
questions.why: 謝謝 (xièxie) = thank you. The usual reply is 不客氣 (bú kèqi), 'you're welcome'.

questions.q: You hold the door open and the office clerk says 謝謝 (xièxie). You reply —
questions.why: 不客氣 (bú kèqi) = you're welcome. 對不起 is sorry, 再見 is goodbye, and 請問 introduces a question.

questions.q: A student says your book is in the 教室. Where should you look?
questions.why: 教室 (jiàoshì) = classroom. Careful with the neighbors: 辦公室 (bàngōngshì) is the office and 教務處 (jiàowùchù) is academic affairs.

questions.q: 校長 refers to the —
questions.why: 校長 (xiàozhǎng) is the principal. 主任 (zhǔrèn) is a department director and 組長 (zǔzhǎng) a section head.

questions.q: After lunch an announcement says 午休. Students are expected to —
questions.why: 午休 (wǔxiū) is the post-lunch quiet rest. Most elementary students put their heads down on the desk for about 30 minutes.

questions.q: Students shout 加油 at a sports day race. They are saying —
opts: Go for it / You can do it
questions.why: 加油 (jiāyóu) literally means 'add oil'. It is the all-purpose cheer — for races, exams, and hard days.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. What is being said?
questions.why: 再見 (zàijiàn) = goodbye, literally 'see again'. Classes often chant 老師再見 at the end of a lesson.

questions.q: An office clerk hands you a form and says 麻煩你. This is —
opts: a warning that the form is wrong
a polite 'sorry to trouble you — please'
questions.why: 麻煩你 (máfan nǐ) softens a request. It is the standard polite lead-in when someone needs you to do something.

questions.q: A young student urgently says 老師，我要去廁所. They need —
questions.why: 廁所 (cèsuǒ) = toilet / restroom. The full sentence 我要去廁所 (wǒ yào qù cèsuǒ) means 'I need to go to the toilet'.

questions.q: You want to ask a colleague something politely. You begin with —
questions.why: 請問 (qǐngwèn) = 'may I ask'. It is the standard polite opener before any question, to colleagues or strangers.

questions.q: The schedule shows 朝會 at 7:50. You should expect —
questions.why: 朝會 (zhāohuì) is the morning assembly — announcements, awards, and often 升旗 (shēngqí), the flag-raising.

questions.q: A student holds up an empty bottle and says 我要喝水. They want —
questions.why: 水 (shuǐ) = water, 喝水 (hē shuǐ) = to drink water. Every campus has a 飲水機 (yǐnshuǐjī), a water dispenser.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. What is being said?
questions.why: 對不起 (duìbùqǐ) = I'm sorry. A lighter everyday version is 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi), closer to 'excuse me'.

questions.q: 課本 refers to —
questions.why: 書 (shū) is a book in general; 課本 (kèběn) is specifically a textbook. 作業 (zuòyè) is homework.

questions.q: As you leave the office someone says 慢走. They mean —
opts: Walk more slowly, you're going too fast
questions.why: 慢走 (màn zǒu) is literally 'walk slowly', but it works as a warm send-off — take care getting home.

questions.q: A colleague waves at 4:30 and says 我先下班了. They are —
questions.why: 下班 (xiàbān) = to finish work; 上班 (shàngbān) = to go to work. Same 上/下 pair as 上課 and 下課.

questions.q: A student asks 幾點下課？They want to know —
questions.why: 幾點 (jǐ diǎn) = what time. 幾點下課 asks 'What time does class end?' — the most-asked question on any campus.

questions.q: A student asks you something in fast Mandarin. The simplest honest reply is —
opts: 我不知道 (wǒ bù zhīdào) — I don't know
我很好 (wǒ hěn hǎo) — I'm fine
我要走了 (wǒ yào zǒu le) — I'm leaving
questions.why: 我不知道 (wǒ bù zhīdào) = I don't know. Pair it with 你可以再說一次嗎？(nǐ kěyǐ zài shuō yí cì ma) — 'Could you say that again?'

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. A student is saying —
questions.why: 老師早 (lǎoshī zǎo) = 'Good morning, teacher', the short form of 老師早安. You will hear it dozens of times before 8am.

questions.q: A teacher calls out 同學們. They are addressing —
questions.why: 同學 (tóngxué) = classmate or student. 同學們 (tóngxuémen) is how teachers address the whole class — like 'class' or 'everyone'.

questions.q: Before heading to lunch the teacher says 排隊. Students should —
questions.why: 排隊 (páiduì) = to line up. You will hear it constantly — before lunch, assembly, and dismissal.

questions.q: A student apologizes for dropping a book. You reassure them with —
questions.why: 沒關係 (méi guānxi) = it's OK / never mind. It is the standard reply to 對不起 and 不好意思.

questions.q: A student says the class is waiting for you on the 操場. Go to the —
questions.why: 操場 (cāochǎng) is the open sports field where assembly, PE and sports day happen. 跑道 (pǎodào) is the running track around it.

questions.q: 圖書館 is the —
questions.why: 圖書館 (túshūguǎn) = library. 借書 (jiè shū) is to borrow a book, 還書 (huán shū) to return one.

questions.q: Your desk is in the 辦公室. This is the —
questions.why: 辦公室 (bàngōngshì) = office. Most FETs share one with the other English teachers.

questions.q: A student falls and scrapes a knee. Send them to the —
questions.why: 保健室 (bǎojiànshì) is the school health room, staffed by the 護理師 (hùlǐshī), the school nurse.

questions.q: Students are told not to run in the 走廊. This is the —
questions.why: 走廊 (zǒuláng) = corridor or hallway. You will hear 走廊不要跑 (don't run in the corridor) constantly.

questions.q: 樓梯 refers to the —
questions.why: 樓梯 (lóutī) = stairs. 三樓 (sān lóu) is the third floor; Taiwan counts the ground floor as 一樓.

questions.q: The graduation ceremony is in the 禮堂. This is the —
questions.why: 禮堂 (lǐtáng) is the assembly hall used for ceremonies and performances. Many schools call theirs the 活動中心 (huódòng zhōngxīn).

questions.q: A student is asked to wipe the 黑板. This is the —
questions.why: 黑板 (hēibǎn) = blackboard; a whiteboard is 白板 (báibǎn). 板擦 (bǎncā) is the board eraser.

questions.q: 書包 is a —
questions.why: 書包 (shūbāo) = schoolbag. Taiwanese primary students carry theirs to and from school every day, 聯絡簿 inside.

questions.q: A student has forgotten their 鉛筆. They need a —
questions.why: 鉛筆 (qiānbǐ) = pencil. 原子筆 (yuánzǐbǐ) is a ballpoint pen and 尺 (chǐ) a ruler.

questions.q: 橡皮擦 is used to —
questions.why: 橡皮擦 (xiàngpícā) = eraser. Younger students will hold one up and say 老師，我沒有橡皮擦.

questions.q: The teacher asks students to hand in their 作業. This is their —
questions.why: 作業 (zuòyè) = homework or assignment. 交作業 (jiāo zuòyè) is to hand it in.

questions.q: You say 坐下 to a standing class. You are telling them to —
questions.why: 坐下 (zuòxià) = sit down. The polite classroom pair is 起立 (qǐlì, stand) and 坐下 (sit).

questions.q: 站起來 asks students to —
questions.why: 站起來 (zhàn qǐlái) = stand up. 起立 (qǐlì) is the more formal version used before a class greeting.

questions.q: The homeroom teacher calls out 安靜. Students should —
questions.why: 安靜 (ānjìng) = quiet. 安靜一點 (ānjìng yìdiǎn) softens it to 'a bit quieter, please'.

questions.q: You ask the class to 舉手 if they understand. They should —
questions.why: 舉手 (jǔshǒu) = raise your hand. Very useful for a quick check: 懂的舉手 (hands up if you understand).

questions.q: You want the class to repeat a word after you. You say —
questions.why: 跟我念 (gēn wǒ niàn) = repeat after me. It is the single most useful classroom phrase for a language teacher.

questions.q: A student answers too softly. You encourage them with —
questions.why: 大聲一點 (dàshēng yìdiǎn) = a bit louder. Its opposite is 小聲一點 (xiǎoshēng yìdiǎn).

questions.q: You need the class's attention on the board. You say —
questions.why: 看這裡 (kàn zhèlǐ) = look over here. 看黑板 (kàn hēibǎn) means look at the board.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. A colleague passing your desk at 7:40 is saying —
questions.why: 早 (zǎo) is the clipped everyday 'morning' — shorter and far more common than 早安 between colleagues.

questions.q: 放學 is the moment when —
questions.why: 放學 (fàngxué) = school lets out. Compare 上學 (shàngxué), to go to school.

questions.q: 早自習 is —
questions.why: 早自習 (zǎozìxí) is the quiet study slot before the first period — reading, correcting homework, sometimes English morning activities.

questions.q: 升旗 on Monday morning is the —
questions.why: 升旗 (shēngqí) is the flag-raising that opens the weekly assembly, usually with the national anthem.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The class is saying —
questions.why: 謝謝老師 (xièxie lǎoshī) = thank you, teacher — chanted together at the end of a lesson.

questions.q: 午餐 is —
questions.why: 午餐 (wǔcān) = lunch. 營養午餐 (yíngyǎng wǔcān) is the school lunch program served in every Taiwanese school.

questions.q: A student points at your lunch and says 好吃嗎？They are asking —
questions.why: 好吃 (hǎochī) = delicious, for food you chew. For drinks use 好喝 (hǎohē).

questions.q: The 飲水機 is where you —
questions.why: 飲水機 (yǐnshuǐjī) is the hot-and-cold water dispenser found on every floor of a Taiwanese school.

questions.q: 垃圾桶 is the —
questions.why: 垃圾桶 (lèsètǒng) = rubbish bin. Taiwanese schools separate carefully: 回收 (huíshōu) is recycling and 廚餘 (chúyú) food waste.

questions.q: A colleague finishes explaining the timetable. To show you followed it, say —
questions.why: 我懂了 (wǒ dǒng le) = I've got it. If you haven't, 我不懂 (wǒ bù dǒng) is perfectly polite.

questions.q: You missed what someone said. The natural request is —
opts: 再說一次 (zài shuō yí cì)
questions.why: 再說一次 (zài shuō yí cì) = say it once more. Soften it with 可以再說一次嗎？(kěyǐ zài shuō yí cì ma).

questions.q: A student asks 今天星期幾？They want to know —
opts: what day of the week it is
questions.why: 星期幾 (xīngqí jǐ) = which day of the week. 星期一 is Monday through 星期六 Saturday, and Sunday is 星期日 or 星期天.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. What has just happened?
questions.why: 下課了 (xiàkè le) = class is over. The 了 marks the change — it has just now happened.

questions.q: The 護理師 works in the health room. They are the —
questions.why: 護理師 (hùlǐshī) is the school nurse. The older word 護士 (hùshì) is still widely heard.

questions.q: The 警衛 sits at the front gate. They are the —
questions.why: 警衛 (jǐngwèi) is the gate guard who signs visitors in. Say 早 to them and you'll be greeted every morning.

questions.q: You knock on the office door and hear 請進. You should —
questions.why: 請進 (qǐng jìn) = please come in. Its partner is 請坐 (qǐng zuò), please sit down.

questions.q: 請坐 invites you to —
questions.why: 請坐 (qǐng zuò) = please sit. In an office you'll usually hear it together with 喝茶 (hē chá), have some tea.

questions.q: 生日 means —
questions.why: 生日 (shēngrì) = birthday. 生日快樂 (shēngrì kuàilè) is happy birthday — you will sing it a lot.

questions.q: A colleague has just had good news. You say —
questions.why: 恭喜 (gōngxǐ) = congratulations. At Lunar New Year you'll hear the doubled 恭喜恭喜 everywhere.

questions.q: A parent phones to say their child 生病了. The child is —
questions.why: 生病 (shēngbìng) = to fall ill. The parent will usually follow with 今天請假 — taking the day off.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your co-teacher has just turned to the class and asked —
questions.why: 對不對？(duì bú duì) = right? / correct? It is the standard tag question Taiwanese teachers use to check a class is with them.

questions.q: 你叫什麼名字？asks for your —
questions.why: 名字 (míngzi) = name. To answer: 我叫… (wǒ jiào…), 'I'm called…'.

questions.q: A young student asks you 你幾歲？They want to know your —
questions.why: 幾歲 (jǐ suì) = how old. Children ask it freely; it is curiosity, not rudeness.

questions.py: nǐ shì nǎ yì guó rén?
questions.q: 你是哪一國人？asks —
questions.why: 哪一國人 (nǎ yì guó rén) = which country's person. Answer with 我是…人, e.g. 我是美國人 (wǒ shì Měiguó rén).

questions.q: A student answers a hard question. You praise them with —
questions.why: 好厲害 (hǎo lìhài) = impressive / amazing. Also common: 很棒 (hěn bàng) and 太好了 (tài hǎo le).

questions.q: 很棒 is used to say something is —
questions.why: 很棒 (hěn bàng) = great, well done. 你很棒 (nǐ hěn bàng) is warm praise for a student.

questions.q: It's pouring and a student has no 雨傘. They have no —
questions.why: 雨傘 (yǔsǎn) = umbrella. A rain cape, worn over the schoolbag, is a 雨衣 (yǔyī).

questions.q: The announcement says 下雨, so assembly is canceled. It is —
questions.why: 下雨 (xià yǔ) = to rain. On rainy days 朝會 moves indoors or is skipped altogether.

questions.q: A colleague points at a wet floor and says 小心. They mean —
questions.why: 小心 (xiǎoxīn) = be careful, watch out. You'll see it on 小心地滑 signs — careful, slippery floor.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your co-teacher has just said —
questions.why: 開始 (kāishǐ) = to begin. Its opposite in class is 停 (tíng), stop.

questions.q: Someone calls you as you rush off. 等一下 means —
questions.why: 等一下 (děng yíxià) = wait a moment. Repeated as 等一下等一下 it just means 'hang on, hang on'.

questions.q: 今天 means —
questions.why: 今天 (jīntiān) = today. The set is 昨天 (zuótiān) yesterday, 今天 today, 明天 (míngtiān) tomorrow.

questions.q: 明天見 means —
questions.why: 明天見 (míngtiān jiàn) = see you tomorrow. Swap in 下禮拜見 for 'see you next week'.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. A colleague is telling you —
questions.why: 上課了 (shàngkè le) = class has started — time to go. Often said with a nod toward the door.

questions.q: 考試 is —
questions.why: 考試 (kǎoshì) = exam or test. 小考 (xiǎokǎo) is a quiz; 段考 (duànkǎo) the bigger term exam.

questions.q: A student anxiously asks about their 分數. They mean their —
questions.why: 分數 (fēnshù) = marks or score. 幾分 (jǐ fēn) asks 'how many points?'

questions.q: A colleague asks if you can help. You agree with —
questions.why: 沒問題 (méi wèntí) = no problem. 好啊 (hǎo a) is an even lighter 'sure'.

questions.q: A colleague is struggling with a heavy box. Offering help, you say —
questions.why: 我來 (wǒ lái) literally 'I'll come' — in practice 'let me do it'. Short, warm and very Taiwanese.

questions.q: The lunch is cooked in the 廚房. This is the —
questions.why: 廚房 (chúfáng) = kitchen. Many Changhua schools have a 中央廚房 (central kitchen) cooking for several schools.

questions.q: 制服 refers to the —
questions.why: 制服 (zhìfú) = uniform. The PE kit is the 運動服 (yùndòngfú), worn on PE days.

questions.q: 運動會 is the school's —
questions.why: 運動會 (yùndònghuì) is sports day — a whole-school event with parents watching and class relay races.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You offered help and got this reply. It means —
questions.why: 不用了 (bú yòng le) = no need / it's fine. A gentle refusal, not a rebuff.

questions.q: You need the 鑰匙 to open the classroom. You need the —
questions.why: 鑰匙 (yàoshi) = key. Ask the office: 我可以借鑰匙嗎？(may I borrow the key?)

questions.q: A student asks you to turn on the 冷氣. They mean the —
questions.why: 冷氣 (lěngqì) = air conditioning; 電風扇 (diànfēngshàn) is a fan. 開冷氣 = turn the AC on.

questions.q: 關電燈 asks you to —
questions.why: 電燈 (diàndēng) = electric light. 開 (kāi) turns things on, 關 (guān) turns them off — 開燈 / 關燈.

questions.q: The line is untidy and the teacher says 排好. Students should —
questions.why: 排好 (pái hǎo) = line up properly. The 好 marks completion — do it and do it right.

questions.q: 回家 means to —
questions.why: 回家 (huí jiā) = go home. 回家作業 (huí jiā zuòyè) is homework — literally 'go-home work'.

questions.q: As a student cycles off you call 路上小心. You are saying —
questions.why: 路上小心 (lùshàng xiǎoxīn) = take care on the road. Perfect for dismissal time, alongside 慢走.

questions.q: 腳踏車 is a —
questions.why: 腳踏車 (jiǎotàchē) = bicycle. A scooter is 機車 (jīchē) — the way most Taiwanese teachers get to work.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your colleague is telling you —
questions.why: 我先走了 (wǒ xiān zǒu le) = I'll head off first. Polite to say before leaving a room of colleagues.

questions.q: 廁所在哪裡？asks —
questions.why: …在哪裡 (zài nǎlǐ) = where is…? Swap in any place: 辦公室在哪裡？教室在哪裡？

questions.q: Pointing at an object you don't know the word for, you can say —
questions.why: 這個 (zhège) = this one; 那個 (nàge) = that one. Point and say 這個中文怎麼說？— how do you say this in Chinese?

questions.q: …中文怎麼說？asks —
opts: How do you say it in Chinese?
questions.why: 怎麼說 (zěnme shuō) = how do you say it. The single best question for learning on the job.

questions.q: Asked if you speak Chinese, you answer 一點點. You mean —
questions.why: 一點點 (yìdiǎndiǎn) = just a little. Modest and always well received: 我會說一點點中文.

questions.q: 交上來 tells students to —
questions.why: 交上來 (jiāo shànglái) = hand it in / pass it forward. 收作業 (shōu zuòyè) is the teacher collecting it.

questions.q: 分組 asks the class to —
questions.why: 分組 (fēnzǔ) = divide into groups. 兩人一組 (liǎng rén yì zǔ) means 'in pairs'.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. Your co-teacher is telling the class —
questions.why: 很好 (hěn hǎo) = very good. Stacked up with 很棒 and 太好了 it makes a full praise toolkit.

questions.q: 錯了 tells a student their answer is —
questions.why: 錯 (cuò) = wrong; 對 (duì) = right. Softer than 錯了 is 再想想 (zài xiǎngxiang) — think again.

questions.q: 對 as a one-word reply means —
questions.why: 對 (duì) = correct / that's right. Doubled as 對對對 it's an enthusiastic 'yes, exactly'.

questions.q: Asked how your first week went, you reply 還好. You mean —
questions.why: 還好 (hái hǎo) = so-so, all right. Very common — Taiwanese speech leans modest rather than effusive.

questions.q: A colleague says 我很忙. They are —
questions.why: 忙 (máng) = busy. 你忙不忙？asks 'are you busy?' — a normal opener before making a request.

questions.q: 好累 means —
questions.why: 累 (lèi) = tired. After a long day 好累 will get you a sympathetic 辛苦了 in reply.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. A colleague at lunchtime is asking —
questions.why: 吃飽了嗎？(chī bǎo le ma) = have you eaten your fill? It works as a genuine question and as a warm greeting.

questions.q: You ask where the 教具 are kept. You mean the —
questions.why: 教具 (jiàojù) = teaching aids — flashcards, puppets, dice. Most schools keep them in the 教具室.

questions.q: 投影機 is the —
questions.why: 投影機 (tóuyǐngjī) = projector. The screen is the 布幕 (bùmù) and the interactive board an 電子白板.

questions.q: 麥克風 is a —
questions.why: 麥克風 (màikèfēng) is a loan word — say it aloud and you'll hear 'microphone'. Handy in a noisy hall.

questions.q: 換教室 means the class is —
questions.why: 換教室 (huàn jiàoshì) = change classrooms — usually to a 專科教室 (specialist room) for music, art or computers.

questions.q: 音樂 is the subject —
questions.why: 音樂 (yīnyuè) = music. The other specials: 美術 (art), 體育 (PE), 電腦 (computing).

questions.q: 體育課 is —
questions.why: 體育 (tǐyù) = physical education. On 體育課 days students come in their 運動服.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The announcement is asking everyone to —
questions.why: 請安靜 (qǐng ānjìng) = quiet please. The 請 makes it a polite public request rather than a scolding.

questions.q: 班級 refers to a —
questions.why: 班級 (bānjí) = class. Taiwanese classes are named like 三年二班 (sān nián èr bān) — Grade 3, Class 2.

questions.q: 三年級 means —
questions.why: 年級 (niánjí) = grade / year level. 一年級 through 六年級 covers Taiwanese primary school.

questions.q: The 班長 is the —
questions.why: 班長 (bānzhǎng) is the elected class monitor who calls 起立、敬禮、坐下 at the start of a lesson.

questions.q: The class monitor calls 起立、敬禮. Students —
questions.why: 敬禮 (jìnglǐ) = bow / salute. The full opening sequence is 起立 (stand), 敬禮 (bow), 坐下 (sit).

questions.q: 點名 is —
questions.why: 點名 (diǎnmíng) = to call the roll. Students answer 到 (dào) — present.

questions.q: During roll call a student answers 到. They mean —
questions.why: 到 (dào) literally 'arrived' — the one-word answer for 'here'. Absent is 缺席 (quēxí).

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. As you pack up after a long day, a colleague says —
questions.why: 辛苦了 (xīnkǔ le) acknowledges the effort you put in. The warmest thing a Taiwanese colleague says at day's end.

questions.q: 影印機 is the —
questions.why: 影印機 (yǐngyìnjī) = photocopier. 影印 (yǐngyìn) is to copy and 印 (yìn) alone is to print.

questions.q: You need more 紙. You need —
questions.why: 紙 (zhǐ) = paper. A4 size is said in English letters: A4 紙 (A-four zhǐ).

questions.q: You need to squeeze past someone in a narrow corridor. You say —
questions.why: 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) covers 'excuse me' and a light 'sorry'. Softer than 對不起, which is a real apology.

questions.q: 謝謝你的幫忙 thanks someone for —
questions.why: 幫忙 (bāngmáng) = help. 謝謝你的幫忙 is the fuller, warmer version of a plain 謝謝.

questions.q: 開門 asks someone to —
questions.why: 開門 (kāi mén) = open the door; 關門 (guān mén) = close it. Same 開/關 pair as 開燈 / 關燈.

questions.q: 窗戶 is a —
questions.why: 窗戶 (chuānghù) = window. On hot days you'll hear 把窗戶打開 — open the windows.

questions.q: Before lunch you hear 排隊洗手. Students should —
opts: line up to wash their hands
questions.why: 洗手 (xǐshǒu) = wash hands. Pre-lunch handwashing lines are a fixed daily routine in Taiwanese primary schools.

questions.q: A teacher on 值週 duty this week is —
questions.why: 值週 (zhízhōu) is the weekly duty rota — gate greeting, corridor patrol, assembly announcements.

questions.q: The office says they will 聯絡 the parents. They will —
questions.why: 聯絡 (liánluò) = to contact / get in touch. The daily notebook 聯絡簿 is built on the same word.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The speaker is saying —
opts: I don't understand what I heard
questions.why: 聽不懂 (tīng bù dǒng) = hear it but not understand it. 看不懂 (kàn bù dǒng) is the reading equivalent.

questions.q: Someone is speaking too fast for you. You ask —
questions.why: 慢一點 (màn yìdiǎn) = a bit slower. Pair it with 請 for extra politeness: 請說慢一點.

questions.q: 快一點 asks someone to —
questions.why: 快一點 (kuài yìdiǎn) = faster / hurry. You'll hear it a lot at 打掃時間 and before assembly.

questions.q: 畢業 means to —
questions.why: 畢業 (bìyè) = to graduate. 畢業典禮 (bìyè diǎnlǐ) is the graduation ceremony in June.

questions.q: 開學 is the —
questions.why: 開學 (kāixué) = term begins. Taiwan's first semester opens in late August or early September.

questions.q: 寒假 is the —
questions.why: 寒假 (hánjià) = winter holiday, roughly late January to mid-February around Lunar New Year. Summer is 暑假 (shǔjià).

questions.q: 暑假 falls in —
questions.why: 暑假 (shǔjià) = summer holiday, July through August. Many FETs run 英語營 (English camps) during it.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The greeting is —
questions.why: 新年快樂 (xīnnián kuàilè) = happy new year. At Lunar New Year add 恭喜發財 (gōngxǐ fācái) for good fortune.

questions.q: A 紅包 given at Lunar New Year contains —
questions.why: 紅包 (hóngbāo) is the red envelope of lucky money. Give and receive it with both hands.

questions.q: 中秋節 is the —
questions.why: 中秋節 (zhōngqiūjié) = Mid-Autumn Festival — mooncakes, pomelo, and barbecues in Taiwan.

questions.q: 端午節 is famous for —
questions.why: 端午節 (duānwǔjié) = Dragon Boat Festival — 龍舟 (lóngzhōu) races and 粽子 (zòngzi) sticky-rice dumplings.

questions.q: 教師節 on 28 September honours —
questions.why: 教師節 (jiàoshījié) = Teachers' Day, marking Confucius's birthday. Expect cards and small gifts from students.

questions.q: A banner at the gate reads 歡迎. It says —
questions.why: 歡迎 (huānyíng) = welcome. 歡迎光臨 (huānyíng guānglín) is the shop version you hear everywhere in Taiwan.

questions.q: Before an event someone says 我們來拍照. They want to —
questions.why: 拍照 (pāizhào) = take a photo. Expect 一、二、三 followed by everyone saying 茄子 (qiézi) — Taiwan's 'cheese'.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. The speaker is —
questions.why: 請幫我… (qǐng bāng wǒ) = please help me… Follow it with a verb: 請幫我開門, 請幫我拿.

questions.q: 開會 means to —
questions.why: 開會 (kāihuì) = to have a meeting. 會議室 (huìyìshì) is the meeting room.

questions.q: 教室在二樓 tells you the classroom is on the —
questions.why: …在…樓 (zài … lóu) = on the … floor. Taiwan counts the ground floor as 一樓, so 二樓 is one flight up.

questions.q: 左邊 means —
questions.why: 左邊 (zuǒbiān) = left side; 右邊 (yòubiān) = right. 前面 (qiánmiàn) is in front, 後面 (hòumiàn) behind.

questions.q: 廁所在右邊 means the toilet is —
questions.why: 右邊 (yòubiān) = on the right. 直走 (zhí zǒu) means go straight and 轉 (zhuǎn) means turn.

questions.q: A colleague explains a change to your timetable. You acknowledge with —
opts: 我先走了 (wǒ xiān zǒu le)
questions.why: 我知道了 (wǒ zhīdào le) = got it, understood. The 了 signals you now know what you didn't before.

questions.q: 手機 is a —
questions.why: 手機 (shǒujī) = mobile phone. Most schools ask students to hand theirs in at the start of the day.

questions.q: 電腦 means —
questions.why: 電腦 (diànnǎo) literally 'electric brain' = computer. 電腦教室 is the computer room.

questions.q: A student says 我沒帶課本. They —
questions.why: 沒帶 (méi dài) = didn't bring it. Distinct from 沒有 (méi yǒu), which means don't have one at all.

questions.q: 我可以借嗎？asks —
questions.why: 借 (jiè) covers both borrow and lend. 借我 (jiè wǒ) = lend me; 還 (huán) is to give it back.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You apologized and got this reply. It means —
questions.why: 沒關係 (méi guānxi) = it's fine, no harm done. The standard, gracious answer to 對不起.

questions.q: 生字 in a Chinese lesson are —
questions.why: 生字 (shēngzì) literally 'unfamiliar characters' — the new vocabulary of a lesson. 生詞 (shēngcí) is new words.

questions.q: 念一次 asks a student to —
questions.why: 念 (niàn) = to read aloud or recite. 讀 (dú) is to read more generally, 寫 (xiě) to write.

questions.q: 寫下來 tells students to —
questions.why: 寫 (xiě) = to write; 下來 marks it as recorded. 寫作業 = to do written homework.

questions.q: 帶回家 tells students to —
questions.why: 帶回家 (dài huí jiā) = take it home. 帶來 (dài lái) is the opposite, bring it here.

questions.q: 太好了 expresses —
questions.why: 太好了 (tài hǎo le) = that's wonderful. 太…了 is the all-purpose intensifier: 太貴了 (too expensive), 太累了 (so tired).

questions.q: 你喜歡台灣嗎？asks whether you —
questions.why: 喜歡 (xǐhuān) = to like. You will be asked this in your first week — 我很喜歡台灣 always lands well.

questions.q: 你會說中文嗎？asks whether you —
questions.why: 會 (huì) marks a learned ability. 我會說一點點 = I can speak a little.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. You offered a second helping of lunch and got —
questions.why: 謝謝，不用了 = 'thanks, but no need'. Refusing food politely usually pairs 謝謝 with 不用了.

questions.q: 好熱 means —
questions.why: 熱 (rè) = hot; 冷 (lěng) = cold. Come Changhua's summer, 好熱 is the campus greeting.

questions.q: 今天很冷 says today is —
questions.why: 冷 (lěng) = cold. Taiwanese classrooms are rarely heated, so winter mornings really do earn a 好冷.

questions.q: You are asked to 帶隊 to the hall. You should —
opts: lead the class there in line
questions.why: 帶隊 (dàiduì) = lead the group. Teachers walk their class in line to assembly, lunch and the school gate.

questions.q: 校門口 is the —
questions.why: 校門口 (xiàomén kǒu) is the front gate, where the 警衛 sits and where teachers greet students each morning.

questions.q: 再麻煩你 at the end of a request means —
opts: sorry to bother you once more — thanks in advance
questions.why: 再麻煩你 (zài máfan nǐ) is a soft closing on a request, roughly 'thanks in advance for handling it'.

questions.q: A student receives a 獎狀 at assembly. This is a —
questions.why: 獎狀 (jiǎngzhuàng) is a printed award certificate, handed out at 朝會 and taken home proudly.

questions.q: 加分 means to —
questions.why: 加分 (jiāfēn) = add points; 扣分 (kòufēn) = deduct them. Great for classroom team games.

questions.q: 🔊 Listen. A teacher is telling a student —
questions.why: 你好棒 (nǐ hǎo bàng) = you're great. The most-used praise phrase in Taiwanese primary classrooms.

questions.q: 注意 tells you to —
questions.why: 注意 (zhùyì) = pay attention, take note. 注意安全 (zhùyì ānquán) = mind your safety.

questions.q: 操場集合 tells students to —
questions.why: 集合 (jíhé) = to assemble / gather. Announced before assembly, drills and sports day events.

questions.q: After assembly the teacher calls 解散. Students may —
opts: disperse and go back to class
questions.why: 解散 (jiěsàn) = dismissed / break up. The counterpart to 集合, and the sound of freedom after assembly.

questions.q: You finish a short talk at assembly. You close with —
questions.why: 謝謝大家 (xièxie dàjiā) = thank you, everyone. 大家 (dàjiā) means 'everybody' and is the standard way to address a crowd.
